THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT

The insurer of the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA.15 Q.0074 is before this Court through this appeal challenging the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Chikkamagaluru, in MVC No.288/2019 dated 23.02.2021.
2.
Heard Sri.Anup Seetharama Rao, learned counsel for appellant/insurance company.
Despite service of notice, the respondents did not choose to contest.

Making the submission with regard to the merits of the matter, Sri.Anup Seetharama Rao,
learned counsel for the appellant contends that respondent No.1/claimant indeed is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The terms and conditions of the policy are clear that the policy covers 3rd party risks only.
Thus, the claimant i.e. respondent No.1 herein being the owner of the offending vehicle cannot claim compensation from the insurer of the said vehicle, i.e. appellant herein.

However,
without appreciating the said fact, the Tribunal awarded compensation in favour of respondent No.1/claimant and ordered the appellant/insurance company to pay the same and being aggrieved by the order thus passed, this appeal is filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel Sri.Anup Seetharama Rao during the course of submission brought to the notice of this Court the points elicited through the cross-examination of PW1 i.e. respondent No.1/claimant.

Basing his submission upon the translated copy of the deposition, learned counsel states that PW1 admitted that the offending motor cycle belongs to him and that he purchased the same three months prior to the date of accident.
Basing on the said evidence, the learned counsel NC: 2024:KHC:45218 states that the insurance company should be exonerated from liability.

5. When the translated copy of the deposition of PW1 is meticulously perused, it is found that PW1 though stated that he purchased the offending vehicle three months prior to the date of accident, his version is that he paid cash of Rs.30,000/- and he has to repay the loan of Rs.20,000/- and thereafter the Finance Company would transfer the RC in his name.
Thus, it is clear that the ownership was not transferred to respondent No.1/claimant by the date of accident.

Keeping the said observation apart, when the written statement filed by the insurance company i.e. appellant herein is gone through, this Court finds that the plea raised in this appeal and the ground urged regarding liability was not taken by the insurance company in its pleading i.e. written statement.

6. In case the stand of the insurance company was that the claimant was the owner of the offending vehicle and therefore the risk of the said owner is not covered under the terms and conditions of the policy, such a plea in specific should have been taken in the written statement filed.
Even during the course of proceedings, the appellant did not choose to file any NC: 2024:KHC:45218 additional pleadings projecting his version and the defence.
Without a specific plea being taken in the pleadings, the party to the proceedings cannot base its case upon such plea which was not pleaded.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that the insurance company now cannot dispute its liability to pay compensation to the respondent No.1/claimant.
Thus, with the foregoing discussion this Court holds that the appeal lacks merits.
Resultantly the appeal stands dismissed without costs.
